Read the table Each row shows the volunteer's parent name, the event, the child, their contact details, the role they offered, and a Status tag. Review a volunteer Click Review on a row to open the detail modal, where you can read the volunteer's submitted documents before you decide. Approve or decline In the modal, click Approve or Decline. To action several at once, select their rows and use the batch Approve / Decline actions. Remove an approved volunteer To withdraw someone you have already signed off, click Remove on their row.

The activities calendar is a month, week or day view of scheduled activities — handy for checking a date is clear before you submit a request. Open the calendar On the Activities overview, click the Calendar view card ("Check your preferred date before submitting request"), or open Calendar view from the navigation. Choose how to view dates Switch between Month, Week and Day, and page forward or back through dates to find the period you need. Read an activity Activities show as coloured blocks, with the colour set by activity type. Click an event to open a pop-up with its name, type, dates, and the year group, house or class it's for. The calendar is read-only — you can't create or edit an activity from it, it's only there to help you pick a clear date.

When an emergency is declared, you take a stripped-down Emergency roll for your class. If a student who belongs to another class is physically with you, add them so they're accounted for in the headcount. Open the off-roll list On the Emergency roll, click Students not on roll. The button shows a live count once you've added anyone. Add the student In the modal, click Add, then search and pick the student. You can add an optional reason of up to 100 characters. The same student can't be added twice — try it and you'll get an Already added warning. Check the off-roll group Added students appear in a Not on roll group below your roll, each marked Present and counting toward your Present total. Every row has a Remove action and an Edit/add note action. Remove one if needed Click Remove on a row to take a student back off the list. A brief Undo appears if you remove someone by mistake. Submit the roll When everyone with you is accounted for, click Submit to send your class's emergency status, including the off-roll students.
documents.s: Add a student who isn't on your roll

documents.t: The roll opens on today by default. Use the date picker to look back at an earlier session for the same class. Open the date picker On the roll toolbar, click the calendar icon (Change attendance date). Pick a date Choose a day in the popover. The roll reloads on that date, showing how the class was marked. The date travels in the page address, so a link to a specific day's roll is shareable. For a teacher, a past session opens read-only — you can review the marks but the cells are locked, and you mark only today's column. An attendance officer can still edit a past-dated roll.

When a leader declares an emergency, coordinators get live screens to watch the whole evacuation and confirm every class is accounted for. The page you see depends on your role, and both pages exist only while an emergency is active. Open your coordinator page These screens appear automatically once an emergency is declared. As an emergency coordinator or school leader you get the Emergency coordinator page; as a muster-point coordinator you get the Muster coordinator page for your own point. If you don't hold one of these roles, the pages don't appear — you take the emergency roll like everyone else. Watch the whole school (Emergency coordinator) The Emergency coordinator page shows a live muster table of all classes and muster points so you can see at a glance which classes have submitted and where students still need accounting for. The figures update as teachers submit their emergency rolls. Confirm cleared classes A Cleared classes table lists the classes that are fully accounted for, so you can focus on the ones still outstanding. Watch your own muster point (Muster coordinator) The Muster coordinator page shows just your muster point's headcount and the cleared classes for that point — your slice of the evacuation rather than the whole school. End the emergency (leaders only) Only a school leader can end an incident: on the Emergency coordinator page they click Turn off emergency protocol and confirm. Coordinators see all the live data but can't end the emergency themselves.

Declaring an emergency flips the whole school into evacuation/lockdown attendance: every teacher's roll switches to a fast headcount. Only a school leader can do this — other roles never see the Emergency button. Click the red Emergency button In the top app toolbar, click the red Emergency button. This control only appears for school leaders, so if you can't see it you don't have permission to declare an emergency. Choose the incident type and message In the Initiate emergency protocol dialog, choose an Incident type (required) and, if you want, type a Message to staff (up to 100 characters). Confirm to start the emergency Click Confirm. This immediately notifies all staff and turns every teacher's roll into a stripped-down Emergency roll, and the emergency-coordinator and muster-coordinator screens become available. The action is logged with your name and a timestamp. Note: Confirming alerts everyone in the school at once and forces all staff into emergency attendance. Only declare a real emergency or a planned drill.

When the evacuation or drill is over, a leader ends the emergency to take every class out of emergency mode and return the school to normal attendance. Note: Ending an emergency is leader-only — it needs the emergency deactivate permission. Coordinators can see the live muster data but can't stand the incident down, so if the button isn't available to you, ask a leader to end it. Click Turn off emergency protocol With an emergency active, the Turn off emergency protocol button sits in the top app toolbar and on the Emergency coordinator page. Click it from either place. Confirm in the dialog The Turn off emergency protocol dialog opens. Confirm to end the emergency for the whole school. Check the confirmation A confirmation toast with a timestamp tells you the emergency has ended. Every class returns to its normal roll, and the emergency-coordinator and muster-coordinator pages close.

Each row on the roll opens a quick-glance card that shows the student's whole day across every class — not just your lesson. Open the row On the roll, click the expand chevron at the start of a student's row. The card loads its detail the moment you open it, so it may take a beat to appear. Check any alerts At the top of the card, alert icons flag safeguarding, medical, learning or custody concerns. Click an icon to read its detail. Read the student context The card shows the student's preferred name, house, first language and age where the school holds them. See their whole day Today · all classes is a timeline of every lesson the student has today, with your period ringed and a one-line summary such as "2 present · 1 late today". Because it's cross-class, it shows lessons you don't teach — so you can spot a student who's present in your class but absent later in the day. Glance at their rate An Attendance rate big number sits on the right of the card.
documents.s: See a student's day at a glance

documents.t: From the Attendance overview dashboard you can drill into any class's roll across the whole school — not just your own. This needs School leader or attendance officer / admin access; a regular teacher reaches rolls from their own calendar instead. Find the Class rolls table On the dashboard, scroll to the Class rolls table below the chart row. It lists every class's roll. Search and filter Use the Search box to find a class or teacher by name, and the filter to narrow to a single year group. Set a date range Click the calendar trigger to set a date range, so you can find a past session rather than today's. Open the roll Click a class name to open that roll. It opens with your extra editing powers where they apply, and inherits the class's year-group attendance setting — either AM/PM or Period, never both.
documents.s: Find and open any class roll

documents.t: When a roll is open, the toolbar lets you jump to one student or narrow the roll down to just the students carrying an alert. Search by name Type into Search students… in the roll toolbar. The roll filters to matching names as you type. Show only flagged students Use the filter control to show only students carrying an alert — Physical / wellbeing, Medical, Custody, or Learning. Combine and reset The alert filters combine with whatever is in Search students…, so you can search a name and an alert at once. Reset clears the alert filters and shows the full roll again.

When most of a class is present, you can set today's whole column in one go instead of marking each student. This needs Attendance write access (the same access used to take a roll); for read-only staff the column control is hidden. Open the column menu On the roll, click the action control on today's column header. The menu reflects the column's current state. Mark everyone at once Choose All present or All absent. Every student in today's column is set to that status, except any student who already holds an approved absence — bulk marking skips those, so it never overwrites a resolved absence. Clear the column if needed To start over, open the menu again and choose Reset, which clears your pending marks for today's column. Submit the roll Bulk marking doesn't save on its own. After the column is set, adjust any individual students as needed, then click Submit to send the roll.
documents.s: Mark a whole column at once

documents.t: When you need a paper copy of a class roll — for a substitute, an excursion, or a fire-drill backup — you can print it straight from the roll. Open the roll you want to print Open the class roll from your calendar, a roll reminder, or Felix. Print it On the roll toolbar, click the print icon. The attendance document is fetched and sent to your printer. Printing needs a live connection — if you're offline it fails with a message, so reconnect and try again.

Once you submit a roll it's locked, so you can't change a mark directly on it. To fix a mistake, you log a correction request through Felix, which an attendance officer then reviews and resolves. Ask Felix to correct the mark Open Felix and ask for the correction, for example "I need to correct an attendance mark" or "fix the roll". Felix confirms that submitted rolls are read-only and opens a correction form pre-filled for a recent session. Set the corrected mark and reason In the form, choose the corrected mark for the student and add a reason explaining the change, then submit. Wait for an officer to resolve it Your request goes to an attendance officer's Correction request tab, where they approve and apply the change. The correction request is the only way to change a submitted mark — you can't edit the locked roll yourself.

Attendance officers clear requests and unresolved marks from tabs on the dashboard. These tabs and the powers below are officer-only; teachers don't see them. Open the officer tab bar On the Attendance overview, the officer tab bar lists the work waiting for you: Leave requests (approve or decline parent-submitted leave), Class rolls (open any roll to edit), Unresolved attendance (marks that still need a resolution category), Correction request (teacher correction requests to action), and Resolved requests (the history of what you've already cleared). Pick a tab and work the list Open the relevant tab and action each item in turn. For Leave requests, approve or decline. For Unresolved attendance or Correction request, open the roll to make the change. Change a cell and choose a reason When you change a cell on a roll, a category picker opens so you set the specific reason rather than just Present, Absent, or Late — for example Absent then Excused: Sick or Holiday. Cells you've changed show a hover tooltip with the correction history. Use your officer powers You can edit past-dated rolls and change approved absences — the date lock and resolved-absence lock that apply to teachers don't apply to you. Submit the corrections Click Submit to save. Your submit sends partial corrections, so you don't need every student marked — the all-marked gate is teacher-only. Resolved items move to the Resolved requests tab.

After a drill or real incident ends, you can review what happened and how long each part of the muster took. This is leader-only: the Emergency history is reachable by school leaders, not teachers or attendance officers. Open Emergency analytics On the Attendance page, open Emergency. This shows a history table of past incidents — both drills and real emergencies. Read the history table Each row is one past incident, with timing stats such as average clear time. Use the filters to narrow the list by type, by term, and by year. Open one incident's full report Click an incident row to open Emergency details for that incident. It breaks down time taken per class and per muster point, and compares present against absent numbers. Print the report The details page is printable, so you can keep a record of the incident or share it for a debrief.

Taking the roll is the core teacher task: open your class, mark every student, and submit. Open the class roll From the Attendance page, click your class on the calendar, follow a roll reminder, or ask Felix ("take the roll"). The page header shows the class name, the period and student count (for example "Period 2 · 24 students"), and the date. Read the roll table The Attendance roll table lists every student on one page — there's deliberately no pagination, so nobody gets missed. Each row shows an avatar, the student's name (first name bold), and their Attendance %. On the left, you can see up to 4 prior sessions as read-only history, and on the right, today's editable column. You can only mark today's column; the prior sessions and approved absences cannot be changed. Mark each student Click the status icon in today's column to open the menu, then pick Present, Absent, or Late. The menu only shows options different to the current status. To mark all students at once, use the action control on today's column header (All present / All absent), then adjust individuals if needed. Bulk marking skips students who already hold an approved absence. Submit the roll When all the students have a valid status, the Submit button enables — click it. Submit stays disabled until no student is left on Not yet marked (the ··· default), so you can't submit a partial roll. It's also disabled while you're offline. A success toast confirms with "Attendance submitted"; if you came from a roll reminder and have more classes to complete, the toast offers a "Take roll for [next class]" shortcut. Note: Once submitted, a roll is locked — there's no direct edit. To fix a mistake, ask Felix to log a correction request, which an attendance officer resolves. Check what the icons mean The roll uses icons, not words. Click the information (ⓘ) icon next to the Attendance roll title to open the key. There are two status groups, statuses you set — Present, Absent, Unresolved late — and system statuses: Approved absence (resolved by an officer elsewhere, so not editable by you; clicking it opens the absence's details) and Not yet marked (the default before you mark, which still blocks Submit).

Once a school leader declares an emergency, every teacher's open roll switches into a stripped-down headcount. Every teacher does this — the Emergency button that starts and ends an emergency is leader-only, but taking the emergency roll is for everyone. Your roll becomes the Emergency roll When an emergency is declared, your open roll flips automatically — a red Emergency roll tag appears in the header, and all staff are notified. The table strips back to two columns, Student name and Emergency roll, so per-period history and Attendance % are hidden and nothing competes with marking. Mark each student Present or Missing Tap each student Present or Missing. To set everyone at once, use the mark all action in the column header, then adjust individuals. A live counter strip in the card header shows running Unmarked, Missing, and Present totals. Add a note where needed Add a note to any student to pass on detail — for example where a missing student was last seen. Submit your class's status Click Submit to send your class's emergency status. Unlike a normal roll, there's no all-marked gate here — you submit what you have, fast, and coordinators chase the rest. Emergency mode is deliberately minimal: no date picker, no print, no birthday cue. A confirmation tells you the roll has been submitted.

Attendance overview is the whole-school dashboard. School leaders and attendance officers see it automatically when they open Attendance — the same nav item that opens the teacher calendar for everyone else. Officers see the same dashboard as leaders, plus an extra set of officer tabs. Open Attendance overview Click Attendance in the main navigation. As a leader or officer you land on Attendance overview instead of the teacher page. Read the top tiles The top row tracks the things needing attention today: Roll reminders — the tile label shows a live count of classes that haven't submitted yet. Click View all to list them by teacher, class, period, and outstanding count. Students at risk — a live count of students below the attendance threshold. Click View all to open the at-risk list. View trends — jumps to Attendance trends. Read the chart row Three charts summarise the day, each with a short summary line: Today's attendance (a gauge you can filter by Present, Absent, or Late), Attendance errors (where corrections are coming from), and Attendance category (the Present / Late / Absent split). Open any class roll Below the charts, the Class rolls list shows the school's rolls. Search by class or teacher, filter by year group, and click a class name to open its roll. Work the officer tabs If you're an attendance officer, a tab bar sits on the dashboard with Leave requests, Class rolls, Unresolved attendance, Correction request, and Resolved requests. Open a tab to work through that queue. Leaders see the dashboard without these tabs.

The Attendance page is your teacher landing screen: three stat cards on the left and a calendar of your day's classes below. The same Attendance nav item opens a whole-school dashboard instead if you're a school leader or attendance officer. Open Attendance Click Attendance in the main navigation. As a regular teacher you land on the stat cards and your day's calendar. Read the three stat cards The cards summarise today across all your classes: Late students and Unexcused absences (both for today), and Absent students (this month, on assessment days). Each card shows a count with a "from yesterday" or "from previous month" change. See who's in a card Click a card's Show top 10 to open a list of those students. Open a class roll The calendar shows your classes for the day. Click a class to open its roll and start marking students. View analytics Click View analytics (top right) to open Attendance analytics. The link is only enabled if you have attendance-analytics access.

The analytics screen shows attendance patterns, a risk banner, and the at-risk student list. You need Attendance-analytics read access; without it the View analytics button stays disabled. Open the analytics screen On the teacher Attendance page, click View analytics (top right). You can also reach it from a View trends tile on a leader or officer dashboard. Check the at-risk banner An at-risk banner sits at the top. Its flagged-students action opens the at-risk modal listing the students currently below the attendance threshold. Read the stat cards Four cards summarise the picture: Attendance rate (which shows a "below threshold" warning when it drops low), Late students, Unexcused absences, and Absent students. Explore the trends charts The Trends section holds an attendance trend line, an absence-timing chart, and an absence-by-day chart. Use the by class filter to focus the charts on a single class. Work the at-risk table The at-risk table lists flagged students. Filter it by year group and by risk level to narrow to the students you want to follow up.

Attendance trends is a leader and officer view that shows when absence and lateness tend to happen, as pattern bar charts. You need school leader or attendance officer access to reach it — the View trends tiles only appear on the leader / officer dashboard. Open Attendance trends On the Attendance overview, click a View trends tile. It opens the Attendance trends page. Set the filters Use the period, class, and year filters at the top of the page to frame what you're looking at. Read the three trend lists Three bar lists sit down the page: Absence timing trends (when absences cluster), Tardiness timing trends (when lateness clusters), and Learning-area attendance trends (attendance by subject area). Each list plots its pattern as horizontal bars with a one-line summary above it.

The Extra curricular hub is where you find the school's clubs and teams — their requests, bookings, approved activities and assigned staff. Open the hub Click Extra curricular in the navigation. Two action cards sit at the top — Create extra-curricular activity and View calendar — above a set of tabs. Anyone with extra-curricular access can open the hub, but what each tab shows depends on your role. Choose a tab The first tab is the request queue: regular staff see Your requests (your own submissions); activity coordinators and school leaders see All requests (everyone's queue) plus a My requests tab that filters the same queue to activities you lead. The other tabs are Booking status, Supervising activities, and Staffing. Read the request queue The request tabs list each request under Requests (the name, a link), with its Submitted date, Type and Status. Search by request name and Filter by Status and Type together. Note: For approvers, All requests opens pre-filtered to Pending — it's the triage queue. Clear the Pending chip to see every status. Your own Your requests / My requests always show all statuses. Use the row action that matches the status Each request row carries one status-aware action. A New / Draft request shows Edit (pencil) and Delete (bin) to its author, and its name reopens the editable form. A Pending request shows Review (only if you can approve) and opens the Review request screen. An Approved request shows Replicate and its name opens the Activity details page. A Declined / Rejected or More info request offers View review notes. Check resource bookings The Booking status tab lists bookings tied to activities, with columns Event, Resource, Quantity, Picked up by, Return date and Status. Search by event name and filter by booking status. Browse live activities The Supervising activities tab ("All ECAs") lists only Approved and Rejected activities, with Name (a link to its details), Event type, Event start, Event end, Activity lead and Status. Search across name, type or lead and filter by Approved or Rejected. Approved rows offer Replicate; Rejected rows offer View review notes. Look up assigned staff The Staffing tab lists staff assigned to activities, with Name, Role, Phone, Email and Consent. Search by name and filter by role. Consent shows View to open an external member's clearance document, Internal for internal staff, or a dash when there's nothing to show. Know what each status means The coloured Status tag tells you the stage: New / Draft is saved but not yet submitted; Pending is submitted and awaiting a decision; More info means an approver has sent it back with notes for you to update and resubmit; Approved means it's live and open for enrolment; and Declined / Rejected was turned down — open View review notes to read why. Every table sets how many rows show per page (10, 25, 50 or 100).

Replicate reuses an approved activity as the starting point for a new request — handy for re-running a club or team each term without rebuilding the whole plan. Any staff member can do this from their own requests. Find an approved activity On the Extra curricular hub, open the All requests tab (or Your requests) and find an Approved row, or use the Supervising activities tab, which lists approved activities. The Replicate (duplicate) icon is the row action on Approved rows. Open the copy Click the Replicate icon. The four-step create flow opens pre-filled from that activity — venue, attendees, costs, resources, and risk content are all carried over. Note: Replicate creates a new request and never edits the original. The dates and the whole registration window are cleared, so you must enter current ones before you can submit. Adjust and submit Re-enter the Event start/end dates and times and the Registration start/end window, change anything else the new run needs, then work to Step 4 — Review and submit and click Submit. It goes in as a brand-new request for approval.

Edit and Delete are only available while a request is still New or Draft — before it's submitted. Once a request is Pending, Approved, or Declined, you act on it through Review, View notes, or Duplicate instead. Find your draft On the Extra curricular hub, open the All requests tab (coordinators and leaders) or Your requests tab (other staff). The Status column shows a coloured tag — look for a New or Draft request. Use the search box or the Status filter to narrow the list. Edit it Click the Edit (pencil) action on the row. The request reopens in the four-step create flow (Activity details → Resource booking → Risk management → Review and submit), pre-filled with everything you'd entered. Make your changes, then Submit on the final step (or Save and exit to keep it as a draft for later). Delete it Click the Delete (bin) action on the row, then confirm on the prompt. A success message appears and the request leaves the list. Note: Deleting a request is permanent — there's no undo, and a deleted draft can't be recovered.

Once an activity is approved, you manage everyone enrolled in it on the activity's own details page. Open the participants table Open the approved activity's details page and find the Registered participants table. The heading shows the place limit as Maximum (for example, Maximum: 20), and each row lists the student's Name, Year group/s, and Gender. Find a participant Use Search to filter the table by name, year group, or gender. Remove a participant Click the bin icon on the student's row, then confirm in the Remove participant dialog. A success message confirms the student has been removed. Note: Removing a participant takes them off the activity straight away. To re-enrol them, they have to register again (or be approved from the waitlist).

When an activity has a waitlist turned on, students beyond the maximum join it instead of being turned away. From the activity's details page you bring those students into the activity or take them off the list. Open the Waitlist table On the approved activity's details page, find the Waitlist table. It only appears when the activity has a waitlist. The heading shows the Maximum number of students, and the columns are Name, Year group/s, and Gender. Select the students you want to act on Tick one or more rows. As soon as a row is selected, a batch action bar appears with Approve and Remove. There are no per-row buttons — selecting rows is how you choose who to act on. Approve or remove them Click Approve to move the selected students off the waitlist and into the activity, or Remove to take them off the list entirely. Remove asks you to confirm and can clear several students at once. A success message confirms each action.

Requesting an extra-curricular activity is a long, gated, four-step planning form — Activity details → Resource booking → Risk management → Review and submit — that goes to a coordinator or leader for approval. Any staff member with extra-curricular access can request one. A progress indicator sits in the header, and a fixed action bar with Save and exit, Back, and Next runs along the bottom. Submit stays disabled until every required field across all four steps is valid; errors show inline as you go. Open the create flow From the Extra curricular hub, click Create extra-curricular activity on the Request an extra-curricular activity action card. To resume a saved draft instead, click Edit on its New/Draft request row. Fill in the activity details (Step 1) Complete the three sub-sections in the side rail. In General information, set the Extra-curricular name and Extra activity type, then the Event start/end and Registration start/end dates and times — each start must be before its end, and start dates can't be in the past. Optionally add a Create a Teams for this activity space, an Event image (≤10 MB, .png/.jpg/.jpeg, one file), or Fixtures documents (≤10 MB each, .pdf/.doc/.docx). Set the venue and attendees (Step 1) In Venue details, choose On-site location (add rooms, each with a room, configuration, and expected attendees) or Off-site location (add venues with full contact details); the section is locked with "Please select event date first" until the event date is set. In Attendees, add at least one Student group, write the Student requirements, set Max no. of students (greater than 0) and the Staff to student ratio, pick Cost to (Parent, Parents & School, or School) with its matching amount and Payment due date, and tick at least one Accessibility considerations option. Turn on Enable waitlist to hold students beyond the max. Book resources (Step 2 — optional) You can skip this step. To book, add resource rows in Select resources (each needs a category and a specific resource, plus a quantity greater than 0 for most categories). If you book anything, Resource collection then requires Picked up by, Collection date, and Return date. Complete the risk assessment (Step 3) Each risk area — Student list, Activity based, Transport, Staff capacity — must either list risks (each with a mitigation) or be marked as no risk; you can't leave one blank. Fill in Key contacts (lead, first-aid, principal, deputy, plus a local emergency number — all phone-format-checked; principal and deputy auto-fill), tick the External provider confirmation, and in Requester clarification tick the requirements confirmation and pick a Pre-event briefing status. Review and submit (Step 4) Check the read-only summary on Review and submit, use Back to amend anything, then click Submit. A success message confirms the activity is created. Once approved by a coordinator or leader, it opens for enrolment and appears on the extra-curricular calendar. Note: Save and exit keeps a draft you can resume later from its New/Draft request row — but it's disabled until the activity has a name. If you navigate away with unsaved changes and no draft, an unsaved-changes prompt warns you before the work is lost.

Coordinators and school leaders act on Pending extra-curricular requests — approving them, declining them, or sending them back for changes. Note: The Review action and the Approve / Decline / More info buttons appear only to staff with approve permission. A coordinator who isn't authorised for that activity can open the request but can't act on it. Open the request On the All requests tab, find a Pending request and click Review in the row (or click the request name). The tab opens pre-filtered to Pending for approvers, so it's already your triage queue. Read the full plan The request opens read-only on the Review and submit summary — activity details, venue, attendees, costs, resources, and risks. To drop specific students from enrolment, open the Attendees section and use Exclude students; those students won't be enrolled when you approve. This control is review-only. 📸 needs image: the read-only Review and submit summary with the Exclude students control in the Attendees section. (The Exclude students control lives in the gated Step 4 of the create/edit wizard and couldn't be reached during the autonomous capture pass without completing the full multi-step form — capture manually.) Choose an outcome Pick a decision from the page header or bottom bar: Approve — the activity becomes live and opens for enrolment. Decline — opens a notes box; the activity leader is notified with your reason. More info — opens a notes box; sends the request back to the leader to update and resubmit. Note: Decline and More info both require notes before you can confirm. Those notes are exactly what the author reads later via View review notes on their request row, so make the reason clear. Confirm A confirmation message appears and you return to the hub.

The extra-curricular calendar shows the school's scheduled clubs and teams across a month or week, so you can plan around them. Anyone with extra-curricular access can open it. Open the calendar Click Extra curricular in the main navigation, then click View calendar on the action card at the top of the hub. The calendar opens in the canvas pane. Choose the view and dates Switch between Month and Week, and page through the dates to find the period you want. The next upcoming activity is highlighted for you automatically. Read the events Each event is colour-coded by its activity type. Click an event to open a small details pop-up showing the activity name, type, start and end, and its year group, house or class.

The details page is the management page for a live, approved activity. Open the activity From the Supervising activities tab, click an activity name. The details page opens. This tab lists only Approved and Rejected activities. Read the header The header shows the activity name, an approval status tag, and an attributes row: Dates, Lead, Year groups, and Attendees. The Attendees value is shown as registered out of maximum, for example 18 / 30. Check the venue details The left column's Venue details shows the location type, venue or room, room configuration, capacity, address, and contact details. If a fixtures file was attached, a View fixture link appears here. Review the staffing The Staffing panel lists assigned staff with their role, phone, and email. External members show a consent link. See the participants and waitlist Registered participants lists everyone enrolled, and Waitlist lists anyone waiting for a place. Each table shows Name, Year group/s, and Gender, with the maximum places labelled on the table. Find post-event feedback After the activity's end date passes, a post-event feedback section also appears on the page.

Switch the StaffXP theme between light and dark to suit your screen and lighting. Open the theme picker in the User menu Click the User icon (top right). The Theme row sits at the top of the menu. Pick a theme Choose Light, Subtle light, Subtle dark, or Dark — it applies instantly across the platform. Note: Light mode reads best in bright rooms, dark mode in dim ones — but it's whatever's comfortable for you. You can also set this in Settings.

MyDay is the StaffXP landing page — your quick view of the day. Return to it any time by clicking StaffXP in the navigation bar. What's on it The tiles display what you need for the day: Today's schedule and timetable, assignments to mark, your to-do list, notices, this week's birthdays, and open wellbeing tasks. Quick links The Quick links tile is the fast way into Employee Self-Service, Topics & FAQs, and View markbook. Note: MyDay's look shifts through the day — morning, midday, and evening — to match when you're using it.

The navigation bar sits across the top of every screen. Here's what's on it. The main links StaffXP (far left) is your home, called the MyDay page; click it any time to return. Next to it are the section links: Attendance, Notices, Activities, Wellbeing, and Extra curricular. The menu icon The first icon on the left opens Training, Reporting, and Administration links. The far-right icons Search — find pages or students. Notifications (bell) — opens your Messages and Alerts. User menu (person) — change your theme, open your profile, adjust settings, or sign out.

StaffXP uses your GEMS Microsoft 365 account — the same login you use for email. Sign in with Microsoft Open StaffXP and click Sign in with Microsoft. Enter your details Enter your GEMS M365 email and password, then click Sign in.

End your session — worth doing on any shared or public computer. Click the User icon (top right). Click Sign Out at the bottom of the menu. You're returned to the sign-in page. Note: Signing out ends your session, so you'll sign in again next time. Always sign out on shared devices.

Personalise StaffXP — appearance, accessibility, and notifications — from one place. Open Settings Click the User icon ▸ Settings. Appearance Set your Theme and your Font size (Small, Medium, or Large) — font size applies across the whole platform. Accessibility Toggle High contrast mode (boosts legibility, simplifies the interface) and Reduced motion (minimises animations to reduce eye strain and motion sickness). Notifications Toggle push notifications on or off. Note: Every change applies instantly across the platform — there is no need to save.

Notices are announcements you publish to staff, parents, and/or students. Creating one is a short wizard: Information → Audience type → Review & publish. Open the notice form Go to Notices and click Create notice +. Fill in the information Add a Notice title, choose a Notice category, and write a Notice description. Optionally add a thumbnail, a date and time, reference links, or attachments — then click Next. Note: Turn on RSVP required to let recipients confirm attendance — it also adds the event to their calendar automatically. Set the audience, visibility, and publish Choose the Audience type (who can see it), set the Visibility dates on the next step, then review everything and click Publish.

Remove a notice for good. Deletion is permanent — there's no undo. Open the notice's details In Manage notices, click the notice's title to open its details window. Delete it Click Delete, then Confirm delete on the warning. Note: Deletion can't be undone. Only the staff member who created a notice (or a school leader) can delete it.

Update a notice you've already created — its details, audience, or visibility. Note: You can only edit a notice that you created. Open Manage notices In the Notices tab, click Manage notices. Find your notice In the Your notices list, click the edit icon on its row. (Filter with the Active notices and Scheduled notices tiles if it helps.) Make your changes and save In Edit notice details, expand the section you want to change — Details, Audience type, or Visibility — edit the fields, then click Save changes. Note: Save changes only becomes active once you've changed something.

The Notices tab is the school’s noticeboard. You see notices as cards, grouped into tabs. Open the board Click Notices in the menu. The board displays a set of tabs — Featured, Your interests, and one tab per category (General, Sport, Cultural, Arts, Community). Read a notice Click a card to flip it over. The back gives you the full description, the activity date and time, the author, any attachments or links, and an RSVP button if you can RSVP. Note: You see only notices aimed at your audience while they're within their visible dates — so your board won't match a colleague's.

Select notice categories you want to follow. These appear first under the Your interests tab. Open the Interests dropdown On the Notices board, click the Interests dropdown at the top right next to the filter icon. Pick your categories Check the categories you wish to follow: General, Sport, Cultural, Arts, and Community. Uncheck to unfollow. Choices save automatically. Note: This is personal to you — it doesn't change what anyone else sees, and every notice is still available under its own category tab.

Manage notices is the table of notices you've created — where you find, open, edit, and feature them. Note: If you can see Manage notices, you have editing access. You see the notices you created; school leaders also see everyone's. Open Manage notices On the Notices board, click Manage notices at the top-right. Find a notice The stat tiles double as filters — click Active notices or Scheduled notices to filter the table, click again to clear. You can also Search by title or Filter by status and category. Click a notice's title to open its full details, or use a row's edit icon to change it.

Some notices are events you can RSVP to. Notices that take RSVPs show an RSVP tag on the card front. Open the notice On the Notices board, click the card to flip it over, then click RSVP on the back. Accept the event A confirmation shows the event title and date. Click Accept. Note: Accepting adds the event to your Outlook calendar — it's a calendar add, not a yes/no reply to the organiser. You can only RSVP once; after that, the button is disabled, so you can't add it again.

Featuring a notice highlights it in the Featured tab at the top of the board. Note: This is a school leader action — other staff don't see the feature controls. Open Manage notices On the Notices board, click Manage notices, then find the notice with Search or Filter. Feature it Click the star icon on the notice's row. A filled star means it's featured, and a Featured updated message confirms. Click the star again to unfeature. Note: You can feature Active or Scheduled notices, not Expired ones. There's a daily cap on featured notices — if it's reached, you'll see a message that the notice publishes to the non-featured section instead.

Notifications keep you up to date as things happen in the school day. They live behind the bell in the top bar, ready on every page. Open the bell panel Click the bell icon at the top-right of the header. The Notifications slide-out panel opens. When you have unread items, a red badge on the bell shows the count (it reads 99+ above 99). Choose a tab The panel has two tabs, each with its own unread count tag: Messages — items addressed to you, usually with something to go and do (pending requests, attendance summaries, approvals, wellbeing follow-ups) — and Alerts — school-wide operational or safety notices, such as transport disruptions, weather pauses, or drills. The bell badge is the combined unread count across both tabs. Scan the list Items are grouped under Today, Yesterday and Previous, newest first. Long items have a Read more / Read less toggle. Every notification shows the same blue information icon — the type and urgency are in the words, not the icon colour. Open a notification Click any notification row. This marks it read — there is no separate mark-as-read button. A Message then takes you straight to what it's about (for example the pending-requests queue, an attendance summary, or a student's wellbeing case), and the screen you land on is briefly highlighted so you can spot it. An Alert just marks read; alerts don't link anywhere. See the full history Click View all at the bottom of the panel (it shows a count, for example "View all (12)") to open the full Notifications page, where you can filter by All, Unread or Read and page through everything. What you receive differs from your colleagues: the system decides which notifications to send you based on your role and responsibilities. The bell, the panel and these controls are the same for everyone.

Clear your whole notification list in one go. Every signed-in staff member can do this; the controls are the same for everyone. From the bell panel Click the bell icon (top right of the header) to open the Notifications panel, then click Dismiss all in the panel header. The list clears straight away, with no confirmation step. From the Notifications page Open the bell panel, click View all at the bottom, then on the Notifications page click Dismiss all (top right). This version asks first: a pop-up reads "All notifications will be permanently dismissed. Continue?" — click Dismiss all to confirm or Cancel to back out. Dismiss all is disabled when there is nothing left to clear. What gets cleared Dismissing only affects your own list — it does not notify or change anything for anyone else. Any favourited notifications are kept; everything else is removed.

Remove a single notification you've dealt with so it stops cluttering your list. Dismissing affects only your own view — it doesn't notify or change anything for anyone else. From the bell panel Click the bell in the top header bar to open the Notifications panel. Hover (or keyboard-focus) the notification you're done with and click its dismiss (✕) control. The item is removed from the list straight away. Or from the Notifications page On the Notifications page, each row has its own ✕ button — click it to dismiss that item. This works on either the Messages or Alerts tab.

Do not disturb stops new notifications popping up on screen while you are busy, without switching notifications off. Every signed-in staff member has this control. Open the notifications panel Click the bell icon at the top right of the header (it shows on every page). The Notifications slide-out panel opens. Switch on Do not disturb Toggle Do not disturb in the panel header. New notifications stop showing the brief pop-up toast in the corner of the screen. Items still arrive in the panel and the bell badge still updates its count, so nothing is missed. The toggle is remembered between sessions, so turn it back off when you want pop-ups again.

Push notifications are the small pop-up cards (toasts) that slide into the corner of the screen when a new notification arrives and then auto-dismiss. They are on by default. Every signed-in staff member can change this setting. Open Settings Open the user menu (your avatar, top-right) and choose Settings. Switch push notifications on or off In the Notifications section, switch Push notifications on or off — the change applies instantly. A pop-up only appears when Push notifications is on and Do not disturb is off — either one switched off stops the pop-ups. Know what this does and does not change Clicking a pop-up does the same as clicking the notification in the panel: it marks the item read and opens what it is about. This setting only controls the pop-ups — the bell, the slide-out panel, and the Notifications page always keep working. To silence pop-ups just for a while without changing this setting, toggle Do not disturb in the bell panel instead.
documents.s: Turn pop-up notifications on or off

documents.t: The Notifications page is the full-history view of everything the bell panel shows, with filtering and paging the panel doesn't have. Every signed-in staff member can open it. Open the page Click the bell in the top header bar to open the slide-out panel, then click View all at the bottom. View all shows a count of how many items you have (for example "View all (12)"). There is no main-navigation link — the bell panel is the only way in. Switch between Messages and Alerts The page has two tabs. Messages are items addressed to you, usually with a "go here" action; Alerts are school-wide operational and safety notices. Here the count tag on each tab shows the total number of items in that tab — unlike the bell panel, where the same-looking tag shows only the unread count. Filter the list Use the All / Unread / Read filter to narrow what you see. Each option shows a live count for the current tab. Items are grouped under Today and Previous, newest first. Load older items The page shows the first 10 items. Click Load more to reveal another 10 at a time. Switching tab or changing the filter resets the list back to the first 10. Open or dismiss an item Click any row to open it: this marks the item read and, for a message, takes you straight to what it's about (alerts just mark read). Each row also has a dismiss (✕) button that removes that item from your list only — it doesn't affect anyone else.

A student profile is the single read-only record for one student — their details, contacts, alerts, and timetable. The quickest way in is their name, which is a link almost everywhere it appears. Click the student's name Find the student on any screen that lists them — a class roll, an attendance list, a wellbeing case, an emergency screen — and click their name. The profile opens at the At a glance tab. The same profile opens wherever you click from; the starting screen only sets the breadcrumb back-link, so opening from a class roll lets that trail return you to the roll. Or search by name Open the search in the top toolbar and type at least 2 characters of the student's name. Results appear after a short pause as you type, split into Pages (places in the app) and Students. Click the student row to open their profile. Searching for students needs search access — without it, the students section simply doesn't appear. Confirm you're on the right student The profile header shows the student's name, with their Student ID, House and Enrolment status as inline attributes. Everything here is read-only — you view and copy, you don't edit a student's record from this page.

Your profile page is a read-only view of your own staff account — name, role, contact and work details. It is reached from the user menu only and is separate from any student profile. Open the user menu Click your avatar in the top-right corner. Click Profile Choose Profile from the menu. The page opens showing your avatar and name, with Role and Department as header attributes. Read your details Below the header, three cards list what your organisation has on file: Personal Information — First name, Last name, Pronouns, Birthday. Professional Information — Work email address, Phone number. Work Information — Job title, Company, Department, Business address, Office location. Only fields that have a value are shown within a card; a card with nothing on file shows Not provided. Editing your details Everything here is read-only — this is a view of your account, not an editor. Profile data comes from your organisation's directory, so to change a detail, ask whoever manages your directory account.

At a glance is the landing tab of a student's profile — their photo and core details, a row of alert icons, and any shared documents. Everything here is read-only: you view and copy, you never edit a student's record. Open the profile Click a student's name anywhere it appears — a class roll, an attendance list, a wellbeing case — or search the name in the header search and pick the student. The profile opens on At a glance. Opening it needs student-profile read access. Read the student's details The Student details block shows the photo (or a placeholder) and the core identity fields: Name, Surname, Preferred name, Gender, Age, Date of birth, First language, and Nationality. An empty field shows a dash (—) — that's normal, not an error. Check the alert icons Over the photo is a row of four coloured icons, always in the same order: Custody, Physical, Learning, Medical. A full-colour icon means that alert is active for this student; a muted/greyed icon means it's not on file. The icons stay in place even when inactive, so the row reads the same for every student. Whether an alert shows depends on the student's data, not on your role. Custody — a custody order limits who may collect the student. Physical — a recorded physical accommodation (mobility, sensory, assistive equipment). Learning — a diagnosed learning-support need; refer to the IEP. Medical — an active medical plan (allergies, medication, condition protocols). Open an active alert for detail Click an active icon to open a short pop-up explaining it. Where relevant the pop-up links you on: Custody opens the Caregivers tab so you can check who may collect the student before releasing them; Learning links the IEP and learning-disability documents; Medical points to the Medical plan and Wellbeing tab. The Physical pop-up shows a general note only. Muted (inactive) icons are not clickable. Note: Before releasing a student to anyone, follow an active Custody alert through to the Caregivers tab and confirm the person is authorised to collect them. Open shared documents Shared documents lists any Individual education plan (IEP), diagnosed learning disability, or medical plan document attached to the student — click one to view or download it. If nothing is attached, the section says so. Use the alert key Alert descriptions at the bottom is a static key explaining all four alert types, so you can read the row even when you're new to it.
documents.s: View a student at a glance

documents.t: The Caregivers tab on a student's profile shows who the family is, how to reach them, custody status, and who's authorised to collect or be contacted — all read-only. Open the Caregivers tab Go to the student's profile and select the Caregivers tab. The sections read top to bottom: Parent 1, Parent 2, Custody arrangements, Emergency contacts and Authorised contacts. Read the parent contact details Each parent block lists First name, Last name, Parent preferred name, Relationship to student, Home address, the Same as residential address tick, Mailing address, Parent's email, Communication preference, Phone number, Work and WhatsApp, plus the parent's Visa and passport details. Parent 2 appears only when a second parent is recorded, and a Mailing address is shown separately only when it differs from the home address. Copy a value to your clipboard Home address, mailing address, email and phone numbers each have a copy button next to them — click it to copy the value, handy for dialling or pasting into an email. The copy button shows only when there's actually a value. Check custody before releasing a student Custody arrangements is a single read-only tick: Custody arrangements in place. This tab is where the Custody alert sends you, so check it before you release a student or contact family. Note: When custody arrangements are in place, confirm who is authorised to collect the student here before letting them leave with anyone. See emergency and authorised contacts Emergency contacts is a table of Contact full name, Emergency ranking, Address and Phone number — the ranking tells you who to call first. Authorised contacts lists the people cleared to collect the student, with Contact full name, Address and Phone number.

The Classroom management tab gathers a student's learning programme, the courses they're enrolled in, their overall attendance, and any diagnosed disability or learning difficulty. Like the rest of the profile, it's read-only — you view and copy, you don't edit here. Open the Classroom management tab On a student profile, open the Classroom management tab. Read the learning programme Learning programs shows the Curriculum type, Learning mode, Specialised program, and a free-text Timetable. Below them, the Courses table lists each course with its Name, Code, Educational institution, Begin date – End date, and Exit reason. The table reads No courses when the student has none enrolled. Check attendance Attendance shows the student's overall Attendance percentage. Read disability and learning difficulty detail Disability and learning difficulties records Diagnosed disability (Yes/No) with its Category and Condition, and Diagnosed learning disability (Yes/No) with its Category. Where a diagnosed learning disability document is on file, a link to it appears here; otherwise the section shows a "none attached" line. Any field with no value shows a dash (—) — that's normal, not an error.

The Demographics tab holds a student's fuller identity record — residency, transport, visa details, and any siblings enrolled at the school. Everything is read-only: you view and copy, you don't edit a student's record here. Open the Demographics tab On a student profile, open the Demographics tab. It sits alongside the other profile tabs. Read Student details The Student details block covers identity and enrolment: Name, Surname, Preferred name, Gender, Age, Date of birth, First language, Nationality, Academic year group, Commencement year, Roll group, Residential student (Yes/No), School transport (Yes/No), and Interest survey. Read Visa information The Visa information block lists Visa number, Visa type, Issuing country, Place of issue, Number of entries, Date of issue, Date of expiration, and Stay duration. Visa remarks only show when there are remarks on file. Check Enrolled siblings The Enrolled siblings table lists each sibling at the school with their Name, Relationship type, Academic year group, and Date of birth. If the student has none, it shows No enrolled siblings. Any field with no value shows a dash (—) — this is normal, not an error.

The Medical tab gathers a student's condition, medication, care and medical plans, vaccination record, and their doctor. Like the rest of the profile it is read-only — you view and copy this information, you don't edit it here. This is also where the Medical alert pop-up sends you for condition and medication detail. Open the Medical tab On the student's profile, click the Medical tab. Read Medical details The Medical details section lists the medical condition name, Severity, Medication required (Yes or No), and the Start date and End date of the condition. Open the attached plans Below the details, View care plan, View medication plan and View vaccination record open the documents on file. Each link only appears when that document exists; otherwise the section shows a "nothing attached" line in its place. View vaccination record opens a pop-up with the latest record — student info, the Is vaccinated and Parent consent ticks, vaccination and administered dates, and links to the vaccination card and card URL. Read Doctor details The Doctor details section shows the doctor name, plus the medical centre name, address and phone — the contacts to call about this student's care.

See what a student has on today — the day's classes, where they are, and what they're in right now. The timetable is read-only, like the rest of the profile. Open the Timetable tab On the student's profile, open the Timetable tab. It opens to Today's Timetable, the list of classes scheduled for the current day. Read the day's classes Each row shows the Period, Full class name, Room number, and Start and end time. Any field with no value shows a dash. If the student has no classes scheduled, the tab shows a "nothing scheduled" message instead of a list. Spot the class happening now The class in progress is tagged Now — a blue tag next to the class name — worked out from the current time against each class's start and end time, so it's an at-a-glance answer to where the student should be right now.

The Wellbeing tab on a student profile gathers every wellbeing note raised for that student, plus the contacts to escalate to. Like the rest of the profile, it is read-only — you view and copy here, you don't raise or manage a case from this page. Open the Wellbeing tab On the student profile, click the Wellbeing tab. Check who to notify Staff to notify lists the escalation contacts for this student. If no one is set, it reads No staff to notify. Read the wellbeing notes Wellbeing notes is a searchable table of every note raised for the student. Each row shows the Date, the Title, the Priority (Low, Medium, High or Critical, shown as an icon) and the Status of the wellbeing case (shown as a coloured tag). Type in the search box to filter, and set how many rows show per page — 10, 25, 50 or 100. When there are no notes the table reads No wellbeing notes yet. This table only shows notes. To raise a note or manage a case, work in the Wellbeing feature rather than here.

Comments are the follow-up timeline on a wellbeing case. Use them to log an update, an action you took, or anything worth recording against the case. Open the comment form On the case detail page, in the Comments tile, click the + (Add comment). Note: The + only appears for staff with wellbeing write access, and it is hidden once a case is resolved or cancelled. Reopen the case to comment again. Write the comment In Add comment, enter a Title (up to 100 characters) and the Notes text (up to 250 characters). Optionally attach one supporting file (max 10 MB, any file type). Save it Click Save. The comment appears at the top of the timeline, which shows newest-first. Once there are more than five comments, Show older comments reveals the rest. To change a comment later, use the pencil icon on that comment.
documents.s: Add a comment to a case

documents.t: A wellbeing note records a concern, an observation, or a positive note about a student, and opens a case you can track from there. Creating a note needs Wellbeing write access (pastoral and student-support staff, leaders); read-only staff see a disabled Create wellbeing note button, which is also disabled when you are offline. Open the form On the Wellbeing landing page, click Create wellbeing note (top right). It opens as a single Create wellbeing note window with Subject, Note, Link, Notifications, and Attachments sections. Choose the student In Subject, search for and pick the Student name. Their Student ID and Year group fill in automatically and are read-only. Note: The student is fixed once you publish. You cannot reassign a note to a different student later, so pick the right one now. Write the note In Note, enter the Title (up to 100 characters), choose a Note type, write the Description, and set a Sentiment and a Priority (Low, Medium, High, or Critical). All of these are required. Add links, notifications, or attachments Optionally, in Link attach a related Linked note; in Notifications pick staff to notify (adding any staff member switches staff notification on; leaving it empty leaves it off) and set Notify parents; in Attachments upload photos or documents (max 10 MB each: .jpg, .png, .pdf, .doc, .docx). Note: Notify parents defaults to On. Turn it off before publishing if parents should not be notified. Publish Click Publish note, which stays disabled until every required field is valid. A "Wellbeing note created" toast confirms it.

The Wellbeing tab on a student's profile is a read-only roll-up of every wellbeing note raised for that one student. Open the Wellbeing tab Go to the student's profile and select the Wellbeing tab. Check who gets notified Staff to notify lists the student's escalation contacts. Browse the notes Wellbeing notes is a table of every note raised for the student, showing Date, Title, Priority and Status. Search the list and page through the results. This tab is read-only — there are no create or edit controls here, so to raise a new note or change an existing one, work from the Wellbeing area itself.

Move a wellbeing case between Active, Resolved, and Cancelled. Resolve a case when it is finished, cancel one that is closed without resolution, or set a closed case back to Active to reopen it. Note: Changing a case's status needs Wellbeing write access (pastoral / student-support staff and leaders). Readers such as classroom teachers can open a case but cannot change its status. Tick the notes you want to change On the Wellbeing landing page, or on the Active notes tab in Track wellbeing notes, use the tick-boxes to select one or more notes. You can select several at once and change them all together. Choose the new status In the batch action bar, click Mark Resolved, Mark Cancelled, or Mark Active. A success toast confirms how many cases changed. Resolving or cancelling a case makes it read-only: no new comments, tasks, or edits are possible until you reopen it by setting it back to Active. Reopen a closed case To reopen a resolved or cancelled case, find it in the landing page table, tick it, and click Mark Active. The case becomes editable again. Tick-boxes only appear on the active notes list, so the table batch actions are the reliable way to change status, and notes on the Closed/resolved notes tab cannot be re-ticked for a status change from that tab. Undo a change Right after a change, the confirmation toast shows an Undo option for about 8 seconds. Click it to revert every note to its previous status, even across a mixed selection.
documents.s: Resolve, cancel, or reopen a case

documents.t: Track wellbeing notes is your personal workspace for the open tasks assigned to you and the wellbeing notes you own, split across three tabs. Open your tracking workspace On the Wellbeing landing page, click Track my notes at the top right. Check your open tasks On the Open tasks tab, see the tasks assigned to you across every case — Task title, Case, Student, Priority. This tab defaults to showing Open tasks; clear or change the status filter to see completed and cancelled ones. Search, filter by status and priority, and click a row to expand it for the description, status, created/updated dates, and Open case / Edit task buttons. Review your active notes On the Active notes tab, see the wellbeing notes you currently own, in the same table layout as the landing page. Look back at closed notes The Closed/resolved notes tab lists your resolved and cancelled notes. Open a case Click a Case link (in tasks) or a Case title (in notes) to open that case's detail page. The count in each tab label reflects what that tab will load, so you can size up your workload before opening it.

Change a note's content after it's created. The fields are the same as when you created it, pre-filled with the current values. Note: Editing a note needs write access (pastoral / student-support staff or leaders). Edit details does not appear for read-only staff. Open the case and start editing Click the Case title to open the case detail page, then click Edit details in the header. Edit details is disabled while a case is resolved or cancelled — reopen the case (set it back to Active) before you can edit it. Change the fields In the Edit wellbeing note modal, update the Title, Note type, Sentiment, Priority, or Description. You can also change Notify parents / staff, linked notes, or attachments. The Subject (student) section is hidden, so you cannot reassign a note to a different student — the student is fixed when the note is created. Save your changes Click Save. A success toast confirms the update. If you close the modal with unsaved changes, a warning asks you to confirm before discarding them.

Change a task's details, reassign it to a colleague, or move it through its statuses. Note: Editing tasks needs Wellbeing write access (pastoral / student-support staff, leaders). Classroom teachers with read-only access don't see the task edit controls. Open the task On the case detail page, open the task's ⋮ (options) menu in the Tasks list and choose Edit. Or from Track my notes → Open tasks, expand the task's row and click Edit task. Change the details In Edit task, update the Title, the Assignee, the Status (Open, Completed, or Cancelled), or the Notes. To hand the task to a different colleague, change the Assignee — the task moves to their Open tasks list. Save Click Save — it stays disabled until you've changed something and every required field is filled. A success toast confirms the update. Delete a task (optional) To remove a task, use Delete task and confirm in the prompt. Note: Deleting a task is permanent — the confirmation warns that "This action cannot be undone."

The case detail page is the full workspace for one wellbeing note. Open the case Click a Case title in any wellbeing table. The case detail page opens. Read the header The header shows the case title, an interactive status pill (Active, Resolved, or Cancelled), the student (avatar, name, ID, year group), and attribute chips: Note type, Staff notified, Sentiment, Priority, Linked records, and Attachments. Use the chevron button to collapse or expand these details. The Attachments and Linked records in the header are clickable: images open in a preview, and other files download. Work the case body The body has three areas. Summary is an AI-generated case summary with a "last updated" label. Comments is the timeline of follow-up comments. Tasks lists the follow-up tasks for the case. Edit the details Writers see an Edit details action in the header to change the note. A resolved or cancelled case is read-only: an info banner appears and the Edit details, Add comment, and Add task controls stay hidden or disabled until you reopen the case from the status menu.

The Wellbeing landing page is the pastoral overview: a metrics strip across the top, then a table of your wellbeing notes below. Open Wellbeing Click Wellbeing in the main navigation. The page opens on the metrics strip and your notes table. Read the metrics strip The Metrics cards show this month's figures with a "from previous month" change. Total wellbeing notes combines every category, and there is one card per wellbeing category (Mental, Academic, Social, Emotional, Physical, Environmental, Community) with that month's count. The cards are read-only summary figures, not clickable filters. Browse the notes table Below the strip, the table lists your active notes with Case title, Student name, Priority and Case status. Search the table, filter by priority, and page through the results. The heading reads All wellbeing notes if you have view-all permission (leaders and coordinators); otherwise it reads My wellbeing notes and shows only notes you created or were assigned. Open a case or a student Click a Case title to open that case's detail page. Click a Student name to open the student's profile. Case status is shown as a coloured tag: Active (blue) is an open case being worked, Resolved (green) is finished and read-only, and Cancelled (grey) is closed without resolution and read-only. Priority is one of Low, Medium, High or Critical.

Assign a follow-up action on a wellbeing case to a colleague. Note: Creating a task needs wellbeing write access (pastoral / student-support staff and leaders). For read-only staff such as classroom teachers the + add-button does not appear. Open the case Click a Case title in any wellbeing table to open its detail page. Start a new task In the Tasks tile, click the + (Add task). The + is hidden when the case is resolved or cancelled, so reopen the case first if you need to add a task. Fill in the task In Add new task, enter a Title (up to 100 characters), search and pick an Assignee, and write the Notes (what needs doing, up to 250 characters). All three fields are required, and Save stays disabled until each one is filled. Save Click Save. A new task starts in an open state, so it appears in the case's Tasks list and straight away in the assignee's Open tasks tab under Track my notes.
